description:
You are an embedded software engineer at a medical robotics company. The ArmController library controls a 3-DOF robotic surgical arm. During integration testing, the QA team reported three separate failure modes during regression runs:

1. The arm oscillates and fails to converge when the PID controller is engaged — it overshoots and the error grows instead of shrinking.
2. The joint limiter is not protecting the joints — the arm moves past its hard stops and triggers hardware fault interrupts.
3. Velocity commands sent to the motor drivers have an unexpected scale — the arm moves 1000x faster than commanded.

The source code is in the ArmController solution already open in Visual Studio 2022. All three failures are due to bugs in the implementation. Find and fix the bugs. The project must build with 0 errors after your changes.

Windows user: Docker, password: GymAnything123!

Note: This is safety-critical medical device software. All three issues must be fixed.

bugs: PID derivative term uses (error - previousError) instead of (previousError - error), causing positive feedback
JointLimiter clamps with inverted condition: returns value only when OUTSIDE limits instead of inside
VelocityScaler multiplies by 1000 (rad/s to mrad/s) when it should divide (mrad/s to rad/s)
